title: The Night Station
about: The small railway station of Sosnovka, late autumn, night. The last train today, to the regional centre, arrives at 21:40 and stands for two minutes; the next is only in the morning. Two people work at the station: the duty officer and the luggage clerk. In the morning an accountant from the district counts the till. The station has an internal telephone, with sets in every room and on the platform. There is no mobile signal here.

places.name: Duty room
places.about: The duty officer's room with the ticket window: a desk, a safe, the cash book, a control panel.

places.name: Waiting room
places.about: Two benches, a stove, the timetable on the wall, a door to the duty room and the way out to the platform.

places.name: Platform
places.about: One platform under two lamps, cold and windy.

places.name: Luggage room
places.about: A shed at the end of the platform: shelves of luggage, the receipt book, a trolley.

characters.name: Zoya
characters.sheet: You are Zoya Andreevna, 52, the station's duty officer and ticket clerk. A week ago you took forty thousand from the till as a loan for your nephew Saveliy, the luggage clerk: he swore to return it today before night. In the morning the till will be counted. You want the money to be in the safe by morning and no outsider to look into the cash book. You tell nobody about the shortage. Saveliy has not shown himself out of the luggage room all evening. You speak drily and briefly, as your post requires.

characters.name: Gleb
characters.sheet: You are Gleb Ilyich, 44, an auditor of the railway. An unsigned letter came to the head office: there is a shortage in the till at Sosnovka. You came unannounced and sit in the waiting room as a passenger with a ticket for the 21:40 train. You want to see the cash book and the safe before the duty officer understands who you are, and to catch the train: in the morning you must be at the head office. Your official ID is in your pocket, and you will show it only if there is no other way into the duty room. You do not know who wrote the letter. You speak politely and ask questions as if out of boredom.

characters.name: Saveliy
characters.sheet: You are Saveliy, 27, the clerk of the luggage room, Zoya's nephew. She took forty thousand from the till for you, and you promised to return it today. You have only eighteen with you: the rest you gambled away, and you hide that. You want to leave on the 21:40 train before your aunt asks about the money, or to talk her into waiting a week. You have no ticket. You also hide that yesterday you gave the suitcase with tag 14 to the wrong person by mistake. You speak fast and joke your way out.

characters.name: Tonya
characters.sheet: You are Tonya, 31, travelling on the 21:40 train. Yesterday you left a grey suitcase, tag 14, in the luggage room, and you lost the receipt. In the suitcase are the papers for a house, which you are taking to your sister in secret from your husband: you tell nobody where and why you are going, and you do not want to write your surname in the book. You want to get the suitcase without the receipt and leave. A week ago, buying your ticket, you saw through the ticket window the duty officer hand a wad of money from the safe to the young luggage clerk. You will remember this if they start refusing you. You speak quietly and stubbornly.
